column7: Second live occurrence of the -001 defect shape, found by a second unattended final-checks burst immediately after -001's fix landed: core.CreateUser's password-history seed and system_viewer auto-assign (internal/core/users.go) both discarded a returned AssignRole/AddPasswordHistory error but had no panic protection -- a panic on AssignRole propagated through CreateUser, past the already-committed User (and PasswordHistory) rows, producing a misleading 500 (Differing tables: [PasswordHistory User]). Fixed by wrapping both best-effort steps in their own defer/recover, same treatment as -001. Also fixed proactively (no dedicated live finding, but same root cause, single choke point every audit write funnels through): emitAudit (internal/core/service.go) now recovers a panic in its own LogAuditEvent call the same way it already handles a returned error, closing this for every c.Log*/writeAuditEvent* caller at once. Proving test is the fuzz harness itself -- corpus entry 8ee52322e0585924 is the permanent regression for the CreateUser instance; emitAudit's fix is covered by the existing internal/core/server/http/server/grpc -race suites plus TestDirectLogAuditEventCallersAreSafe continuing to pass unchanged. See docs/findings/2026-09-22-FINDING-secret-delete-restore-dependency-emission-panic-masks-success.md
